newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SPIRLEA ADVANCES AT CALIFORNIA WOMEN'S TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPIRLEA ADVANCES AT CALIFORNIA WOMEN'S TOURNAMENT.

text.p: Romanian Irina Spirlea could not have hand-picked a better opponent to face following a three-week break than Elena Likhovtseva.
Spirlea, the eighth seed, rolled past Likhovtseva 6-3 6-3 Monday in the first round of the $450,000 Toshiba Tennis Classic to improve her lifetime record against the Russian to 6-0.
The 23-year-old Spirlea, ranked 12th in the world, recorded four wins this year without surrendering a set to the 25th-ranked Likhovtseva.
"I think we know each other pretty well," said Spirlea following the 71-minute baseline duel. "I think it's hard for her to play me. She has never beaten me and I was counting on that."

After seven consecutive tournaments capped by a loss to French Open champion Iva Majoli in the round of 16 at Wimbledon, an exhausted Spirlea enjoyed time off on a boat in Italy. But she had little trouble sailing past Likhovtseva.

"I don't think I was playing very well but she wasn't playing very well either," Spirlea said. "I wasn't consistent today and it bothered me a lot. I was not match-tough because when you play a lot you get into it. It's like a computer-- You have it and you're not thinking. Now I think stupid things which might cost me the match."

In other first-round play, 14-year tour veteran Helena Sukova of the Czech Republic beat Chanda Rubin 7-5 3-0 when the American retired after having sprained her right ankle trailing 6-5 in the first set. She was taken to a nearby hospital for precautionary X-rays.
Natasha Zvereva of Belarus beat American Kimberly Po 7-6 (7-4) 2-6 6-1 and Sandrine Testud of France ousted Asa Carlsson of Swden 6-1 6-2.
Top seeds Martina Hingis, Monica Seles, Amanda Coetzer and Arantxa Sanchez Vicario all drew first-round byes in the weeklong hardcourt event.
Hingis, who has won eight titles this year including the Australian Open and Wimbledon Championships, is the top seed.

The 16-year-old Swiss world number one ran her record to 50-1 this year by winning the Bank of the West Tournament Sunday. She will play Wednesday night against the survivor of the clash between Argentine Florencia Labat and wild-card American Venus Williams.
Kimiko Date of Japan, who retired at the end of 1996, was last year's winner here.
